newsitem.title: south korea: S.Korean president's son arrested for graft.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean president's son arrested for graft.

text.p: South Korean President Kim Young-sam's son was arrested on Saturday on charges of accepting bribes worth millions of dollars in a corruption scandal that has rocked his father's adminstration.
Kim Hyun-chul was also charged with evading tax on millions more he took as gifts.
Tired and grim-faced, he was escorted from prosecution offices in Seoul after a marathon two-day grilling and driven off at high speed to jail.
Earlier, his father had expressed deep regret for the affair and, in a statement issued by the presidential Blue House, vowed "stern punishment" for those found guilty of corruption.

The junior Kim was charged with taking kickbacks of 3.2 billion won ($3.6 million) in return for business favours from two alumni of his old high school, one a former top executive of a construction company.
South Korea's "crown prince", as he is derisively known, was also accused of evading taxes on 3.3 billion won given to him by business associates, but not as bribes.
He could be jailed for life for tax evasion. Bribery carries a maximum sentence of five years in jail.

The arrest of the president's second son dramatically brings to a head the scandal involving top politicians, bankers and businessmen that emerged from the rubble of the country's biggest bankruptcy in January.

President Kim, swept to power on an anti-graft ticket, has been crushed by the scandal stemming from the collapse of Hanbo Steel Co under five trillion won of debts acquired by string-pulling in high places.

The Blue House statement was released minutes after the arrest warrant was issued in a bid to limit further damage to Kim Young-sam's blighted presidency. Kim's single term expires next February, but he is already tagged as a lame duck.
"President Kim again expressed regrets that the public has been given such a severe shock and disappointment through this incident," the statement said.
"This reflects President Kim's firm intention that there should be no sanctuary when it comes to punishing corruption," it added.
"From now on, President Kim will sternly punish, according to the law and regardless of status or social rank, those linked to corruption."
Kim Hyun-chul would be the first child of a serving South Korean head of state to be jailed.
The charges do not relate directly to Hanbo's failure, which sparked a wide-ranging prosecution graft enquiry that eventually snared the president's son.
Eleven people, including three of President Kim's top aides, are standing trial over the Hanbo scandal.
Kim Hyun-chul is charged with taking 1.7 billion won from the former executive of Daeho Construction Co in return for help in obtaining a lucrative cable television licence.
He was whisked in a police motorcade to the Seoul Detention House, and driven inside past a phalanx of news reporters under the glare of television arc lights.

Former president Roh Tae-woo is in the same prison, serving a 17-year jail term on graft and other charges. Another one-time president, Chun Doo Hwan, is serving a life term in another prison on similar charges.

Opposition parties have accused the younger Kim of laundering, through companies operated by his cronies, as much as 10 billion won of unspent funds from his father's 1992 election campaign. But he was not charged in that connection.
Election slush funds have become a hot political issue for his father, who is under growing public pressure to make a full accounting of his 1992 campaign finances.
Newspapers said Kim Hyun-chul wrote a letter to a friend before being summoned, vowing to "use all means at my disposal to fight any legal prosecution, including arrest". ($1=891 won)
